report_name: Unpatched 'SignDrop' Windows Zero-Day Allows SYSTEM Privilege Escalation

attack_patterns.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack_patterns.description: The SignDrop exploit leverages a logic flaw in the Windows Common Log File System (CLFS) driver to escalate local user privileges to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.

attack_patterns.name: Subvert Trust Controls
attack_patterns.description: The SignDrop exploit abuses the CLFS file authentication mechanism, which was introduced as a security mitigation, to create a file with SYSTEM privileges in an attacker-controlled location, turning a defense mechanism into an attack vector.

malware.name: SignDrop PoC
malware.description: A publicly released proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit for a zero-day vulnerability in the Windows Common Log File System (CLFS). It abuses a logic flaw to achieve local privilege escalation to SYSTEM.

tools.name: Microsoft Defender
tools.description: The SignDrop exploit tricks a privileged process associated with Microsoft Defender, MsMpEng.exe, into opening a malicious CLFS log file. This action triggers the vulnerability in the clfs.sys driver, leading to privilege escalation.

vulnerabilities.name: SignDrop
vulnerabilities.description: An unpatched zero-day logic flaw in the Windows Common Log File System (CLFS) driver (clfs.sys) that can be abused for local privilege escalation to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. The flaw involves the handling of file authentication codes in companion .cnpf files, allowing an attacker to control file creation with SYSTEM privileges.

identities.name: Microsoft
identities.description: Vendor of the Windows operating system, which contains the unpatched SignDrop vulnerability in its Common Log File System (CLFS) driver.

indicators.name: SignDrop LPE via Suspicious CNPF File Creation
indicators.pattern:
title: SignDrop LPE via Suspicious CNPF File Creation
id: f1a2b3c4-d5e6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of Windows Common Log File System (CLFS) authentication files (.cnpf) in suspicious, user-writable locations. This is a characteristic behavior of the SignDrop local privilege escalation exploit.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/new-signdrop-zero-day-exploit-turns.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-13
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.privilege_escalation
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.cnpf'
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - 'C:\Users\'
      - 'C:\Windows\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of CLFS authentication files (.cnpf) in suspicious, non-standard locations, a behavior associated with the SignDrop LPE exploit.

indicators.name: SignDrop LPE via Anomalous MsMpEng.exe File Access
indicators.pattern:
title: SignDrop LPE via Anomalous MsMpEng.exe File Access
id: e2f3a4b5-c6d7-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b
status: experimental
description: Detects the Microsoft Defender engine (MsMpEng.exe) creating or writing to CLFS log files (.blf, .cnpf) in user-writable directories. This behavior is anomalous and could indicate an attempt to exploit the SignDrop LPE vulnerability.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/new-signdrop-zero-day-exploit-turns.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-13
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.privilege_escalation
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\MsMpEng.exe'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.blf'
      - '.cnpf'
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - 'C:\Users\'
      - 'C:\Windows\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects Microsoft Defender's engine (MsMpEng.exe) performing anomalous file operations on CLFS log files (.blf, .cnpf) in user directories, which could indicate an attempt to exploit the SignDrop vulnerability.
